As ever, Donald Trump was transparent about his motive for misleading the American people. He told a cabinet meeting about the “catastrophe” in Spain. “It looks like an invasion of a country. Hundreds of thousands of people,” he said.

“And that same thing’s going to happen to us if the Republicans don’t get elected.” He is worried about the midterm elections in three months’ time, in which the Democrats are currently projected to win both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

He will therefore seize on anything that can be twisted for propaganda purposes into an argument that a Democrat-controlled Congress would be weak on immigration. Hence his use of the scenes from Ceuta, the Spanish exclave on the coast of Morocco, to suggest that Europe has lost control of its borders because of the “very liberal law” of the socialist Spanish government.

Those pictures were certainly alarming and tragic. At least 77 people died when an estimated 60,000 rushed to cross from Morocco to Spanish territory. But President Trump seemed to neither know nor care that these irregular migrants had next to no prospect of making it to Spain proper and the European continent. Most of them, in fact, have already returned to Morocco, many of them voluntarily on finding that they cannot obtain food.

The situation in Ceuta illustrates migration pressures similar to those along America’s southern border. It also illustrates the dangers of misinformation, as it seems that the surge was prompted by fake stories about a recent Spanish court ruling.

But much of what President Trump said on camera and in his post on Truth Social was itself misinformation. There is no reason to link the surge to the policies of Pedro Sanchez and his socialist government, and it is simply untrue to suggest that mainland Spain, or the European Union, has allowed these irregular migrants to enter.

Mr Trump’s intervention is a distraction from a serious debate about how best to distinguish between economic migrants and genuinely desperate refugees, and how to balance a rules-based order with compassion.

This is only the latest of an avalanche of untruths about Europe disgorged by Mr Trump, other senior Republicans and their cheerleaders. They portray Europe as a hellscape of crime and violence caused by mass immigration, facilitated by left-wing leaders.

Any American who has visited Europe knows that it is nonsense, but most Americans have not, and many are ready to believe this kind of propaganda, aimed at undermining support for the Democrats.

There is little that we can do about that, apart from educating the American public. We do our bit. The Independent is a trusted online brand in the United States, and we are dedicated to reporting the facts as we find them.

But there is something that the British government can do about Elon Musk, Mr Trump’s former ally, who uses his ownership of the X social media platform to pump poisonous untruths into the British online media ecosystem.

This may be aimed primarily at an American political debate, but it has an influence on British politics that is unacceptable. Mr Musk’s support for Rupert Lowe, and his Restore Britain micro-party, considered too extreme by Nigel Farage, is an interference in our democracy paid for by foreign money.

Mr Musk has also waded into the Ceuta controversy, posting on X a video from the 2013 zombie film World War Z with the words: “Wow, the situation in Spain looks crazy!” He later clarified he was “just kidding”, but his algorithm-amplified portrayal of Britain as a crime-ridden dystopia has real consequences in our politics. It is time he was reined in.

News.title: Dramatic rescue after woman found clinging to underside of cliff amid raging torrents of California river
News.content:
This is the harrowing moment California authorities rescued a woman clinging to the underside of a cliff after she was swept away by a strong river current.

The woman reportedly fell into the Kern River and was quickly carried downstream on July 25. Kern County Sheriff’s Office deputies and air support conducted a search and found the woman struggling at the base of a steep cliff, partially submerged in the flowing water.

Authorities were able to throw the woman a life jacket attached to a rope and pull her to safety.

Jim Root, guitarist for the heavy metal band Slipknot, has warned followers not to believe everything they read as reports continue to circulate that his bandmate, Sid Wilson, was kicked out of the group.

On Friday, TMZ published a story, citing a source close to the band, who claimed that the DJ and keyboardist, 49, had been “permanently” let go.

Within hours of the report, 54-year-old Root — who joined the band in 1999 — shared a cryptic message on his Instagram Story, seemingly in reference to the rumors.

“Don’t believe everything you read. Stop. Think. Take a breath,” he urged. “Sit with it for a while. Maybe. Just maybe even wait until there’s more information.”

Representatives for Slipknot and Wilson did not immediately respond to The Independent’s request for comment.

open image in gallery Slipknot's longtime guitarist, Jim Root, warned people not to believe 'everything you read' ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery DJ and keyboardist Sid Wilson was previously engaged to Kelly Osbourne ( AFP via Getty Images )

Wilson is among the “Duality” band’s nine classic-era members, having joined the lineup in 1998, ahead of the release of their self-titled debut album in 1999.

He was previously engaged to the late Ozzy Osbourne’s daughter, Kelly Osbourne. The pair began dating in 2022, after 23 years of friendship. They welcomed their first child together, son Sidney, later that year, before getting engaged in July 2025.

They called off the engagement seven months later in March 2026. At the time, People spoke to a source who claimed that Kelly “has been in a challenging headspace for several reasons. It’s been very emotional for her. She’s had a lot going on.”

“Ozzy’s death still affects her deeply. She’s very focused on being there for her mom right now. They’re incredibly close and that’s been her priority,” the source said. “It’s been hard for Kelly and Sid to balance everything, especially with different priorities about where to spend time. This has put a strain on their relationship.”

open image in gallery Slipknot has gone through various lineup changes throughout the years ( Anthony Scanga )

Slipknot was formed in 1995 by three founding members: former lead singer Anders Colsefni, the late bassist Paul Gray, and percussionist Shawn “Clown” Crahan. They later expanded the band by adding seven more musicians, including Sid Wilson, Jim Root, Corey Taylor, Mick Thomson, Craig Jones, the late Joey Jordison and Chris Fehn, creating the nine-member lineup widely regarded as the band’s classic era.

The Grammy-winning band has undergone various lineup changes throughout the years, due to departures, dismissals and deaths. The current lineup is composed of longtime members Root, Wilson, Taylor, Thompson and Crahan, alongside newer additions: drummer Eloy Casagrande, percussionist and backing vocalist Michael Pfaff, and bassist Allesandro Venturella.

Slipknot is best known for hits such as “Duality,” “Psychosocial,” and Before I Forget.” They have released a total of seven albums.

Arsenal fans were left short-changed after the live stream for the Gunners’ pre-season friendly cut off during the first half of the match against Girona.

Kai Havertz had given Arsenal the lead having received a delightful pass from 16-year-old Max Dowman before slipping it past the goalkeeper with a left-footed finish.

Supporters had been able to watch the opening goal, which occured in the 16th minute, before the live stream of the game - airing on Arsenal’s website and app cut off.

Refeshing the page where the match could be accessed - on Arsenal’s pay-per-view tab - only yielded a message that read: “No data available.”

Understandably, fans took to social media to decry their frustration with many voicing their displeasure at paying for a stream they couldn’t access.

“I’m screaming @Arsenal for not being able to use the technology properly,” one user on X, formerly Twitter, as the match entered half-time with the broadcast having been cut off for 25 minutes.

The broadcast cut off around the 21st minute and fans missed Christos Tzolis - one of Arsenal’s new signings - scoring his first goal for the club as he cut in from the left wing to drill a fine effort into the far bottom corner.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

The technical issues didn’t affect all supporters with some noting that the game could still be watched on the Arsenal app though those watching via the Arsenal website seemed to experience the bulk of the issues. The coverage resumed during the half-time break.

Once the live stream resumed on the website and app, the commentators apologised for any issues experienced.

Arsenal’s pre-season fixtures are all available to view on their website and app via a pa-per-view subscription. Each game costs £6.99 to watch individually or there are bundles available. Fans can purchase a full pre-season pass for £14.99 or £9.99 if they paid for an early bird pass which expired at 9am on August 1st.

A grinning Prince Louis donned a Wales bucket hat as he stole the spotlight during a day out with his family to the Commonwealth Games.

In a rare public appearance for the eight-year-old prince, Louis was seen beaming alongside his family with a Beicio Cymru hat - which means Wales Cycling.

William and Kate – who are known as the Duke and Duchess of Rothesay while in Scotland – were accompanied by Princess Charlotte, Prince Louis and Prince George for a netball semi-final at Glasgow’s Hydro arena, ahead of the Games’ closing ceremony on Sunday, in what is the children’s first official visit to Scotland.

Following the netball, the family emerged from the arena between lines of volunteers, and met gold medal-winning para powerlifter Mark Swan and gymnast Reuben Ward on the concourse outside the venue.

open image in gallery ( PA )

Commonwealth Games mascot Finnie also high-fived George, Charlotte and Louis and fist-bumped Kate.

Waiting crowds cheered the family as they made their way to their waiting cars, before they went on to watch cycling at the Velodrome.

Ward, who won a gold medal while competing for Scotland, told Press Association: “Coming into the Games, I was just hoping for the best and hopefully I could get some medals.

“Being in a position where I’m being chosen to meet the Prince of Wales, it’s just a strange but incredible experience.”

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

The family headed to the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome in the east end of the city, where they met Sir Chris himself and took in some of the action on the cycling track.

In recent days, the sporting event – affectionately known as the “friendly games” – has been attended by the Duke of Edinburgh, vice patron of Commonwealth Sport, which delivers the games, and his wife.

Earlier, the King and Queen emerged from a Tardis at the Hydro arena during the opening ceremony.

The light-hearted moment was reminiscent of London 2012 when Queen Elizabeth II appeared to skydive into the Olympic Stadium alongside James Bond actor Daniel Craig.

The opening ceremony in Glasgow was the first to be held indoors as part of a radical restructuring of the games’ finances after Australian state Victoria withdrew as host of the event in 2023, citing spiralling costs.

The future of the event, which originated as the British Empire Games in 1930, was in doubt until Glasgow was convinced to step in and reprise its hosting role from 2014, albeit with significant alterations.

William and Kate will also spend time with athletes competing at the games whose careers have been empowered by the charity SportsAid, which Kate has supported as patron since 2013, and meet emerging talent taking part in the Team England Futures project.

Sporting stars whose early promise was boosted by SportsAid include Sir Chris Hoy, Ellie Simmonds, Dame Jessica Ennis-Hill and Tom Daley.

Team England Futures has given talented young athletes and aspiring support staff the opportunity to attend the Glasgow games to gain behind-the-scenes experience in preparation for potential medal-winning performances as Team England, Team GB or ParalympicsGB debutants.

Jon McConnell’s decision to ditch Love Island to chase gold at the Commonwealth Games paid off as he romped to victory in the men’s 60kg boxing category in Glasgow.

The 23-year-old from the famous Holy Trinity club in Belfast revealed earlier in the Games that he and Northern Ireland team-mate Kaci Rock had applied for the hit ITV show before turning down interviews with the programme’s producers.

McConnell came through a cracking showdown with Orlando Holley-Sotomi of Wales and insisted he would resist the lure of a repeat application in order to pursue a dream of reaching the 2028 Olympics.

McConnell said: “If I hadn’t got through the early rounds, maybe I’d have thought I didn’t make the right decision, but I’ve got the gold medal now.

open image in gallery Jon McConnell of Northern Ireland (left) en route to a Commonwealth Games gold medal against Orlando Holley-Sotomi of Wales (Steve Welsh/PA). ( PA Wire )

“He put me under a lot of pressure but I have a lot of belief in myself. Everybody thinks I’m just this pretty boxer type of thing, but I’m a hard, hard man to beat – and I showed it today.”

Team-mate Rock sunk to a unanimous defeat against England’s Sacha Hickey in the women’s 65kg division, continuing the 22-year-old Londoner’s impressive trajectory in the sport.

Millwall fan Hickey started boxing at the age of six after playing it on her Nintendo Wii. She was taken to the famous Fisher club in Rotherhithe where she soon excelled despite being the only girl.

“I’ve gone from Nintendo Wii to the big leagues,” laughed Hickey, after a dominant performance against her Northern Irish counterpart. “I remember shadow-boxing in front of the TV and somehow I’ve ended up here today.

open image in gallery Damar Thomas won super-heavyweight boxing gold for England (Steve Welsh/PA) ( PA Wire )

“It’s put me in a great position. I’m sixth in the world rankings now and I’ve got the European Championships next, where I’m going for gold. After that it’s all about the World Championships and qualifying for LA.”

England’s Patris Mughalzai won gold in the men’s 65kg division with a unanimous victory over Jacob Cassar of Australia, and Isaac Okoh outclassed Connor Williams of Wales to make it three in an hour for his team at 90kg.

In the concluding session, England took their final gold medal tally to four with Dimeji Shittu outpointing India’s Ankush Panghal at 80kg, and super-heavyweight Damar Thomas dispatching another Indian, Narender Berwal, by unanimous decision.

Ruby White got silver after losing her women’s -51kg final to India’s Sakshi Chaudhary, and Chantelle Reid also took silver at 70kg after defeat against India’s Arundhati Choudhary.

Northern Ireland’s Michaela Walsh won her fourth consecutive Commonwealth Games medal but had to settle for silver after being outpointed by India’s Jaismine Lamboria at 57kg.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel gave glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

Sports.title: Fans fume as Arsenal’s pre-season friendly against Girona suspended for hydration break after unpopularity at World Cup
Sports.content:
FANS fumed as a hydration break was called during Arsenal’s pre-season friendly at Girona.

The first half was momentarily paused on 30 minutes to allow players to grab a drink.



Despite kicking off at 8pm local time, the match began in around 28 degree heat, with the temperature having reached 35 earlier in the day.

The break enabled stars such as Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyokeres and Piero Hincapie, all in the Gunners’ starting XI, to take on water.



But some fans at Girona’s Montilivi stadium were not happy, whistling as players made their way towards the touchline.

And viewers at home also made their views heard, with one asking on X: “Wait, is hydration break now a normal in football? What’s happening?”



A second fumed: “Hydration break in friendlies? This s*** better end when the real season starts.”

Another added: “Why is there a hydration break its pre season c’mon now LADS”.

Boss Mikel Arteta gave his players a team talk as they drank.

The stoppage came immediately after Arsenal had gone 2-0 up, new boy Christos Tzolis adding to Havertz’s opener.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arteta made three substitutions during the hydration break.

Big names Havertz, Gyokeres and Hincapie were all withdrawn – replaced by Marli Salmon, Gabriel Jesus and Fabio Vieira.

Hydration breaks were an unpopular addition at this year’s World Cup in North America

No matter the temperature, three-minute pauses were taken midway through each half in order to allow players to take on fluids.



Some TV broadcasts around the world used them to show adverts, although this was not the case in the UK.

Arsenal have been taking part in warm weather training all week in Catalonia, ahead of today’s match.

Arteta, 44, explained that different schedules have been devised for his players depending on their World Cup workload.

The Spaniard, 44, said: “It is all programmed. We have three different pre-seasons with different groups.

“But the most important thing is not the programme, it is the attitude behind the programme.



“When I speak to Kai, he is desperate to come back tomorrow and Viktor the same and Piero the same.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Tottenham join Newcastle in race for highly-rated Giorgio Scalvini, 22, with Atalanta prepared to sell
Sports.content:
GIORGIO SCALVINI has emerged as a top defensive target for three Premier League clubs.

SunSport understands that Chelsea, Tottenham, and Newcastle are closely monitoring the Atalanta centre-back and have directly approached his representatives to enquire about a deal.



Atalanta have made it clear that Scalvini will not be sold for less than around £42million.

But sources have suggested that Newcastle are prepared to test the waters with a £34m bid.



It is understood that Scalvini wants a move to the Premier League which means personal terms are not expected to be an issue.

The 22-year-old impressed for Atalanta last season, making 30 appearances across all competitions.

His composure and physicality are the two main factors that have attracted Premier League sides to him.

Chelsea recently contacted Scalvini’s representatives to confirm his £42m valuation.

The Blues could launch a bid if they offload some of their defenders.

New head coach Xabi Alonso has already revealed that he wants to sell five centre-backs this window.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

It is believed that Chelsea are in a position to become frontrunners in the transfer race if they can offload players in time.

Meanwhile, Tottenham are currently assessing if the Italian fits their defensive priorities for the upcoming season.

Scalvini could become an option if club captain Cristian Romero leaves in the coming weeks

The centre-back’s profile is exactly what Newcastle are also looking at.

It’s understood the Magpies want a young defender with a high ceiling who is also ready to deal with the demands of the Premier League.



Newcastle have already been in touch with Scalvini’s representatives to ask about the financial aspects.

The club’s sporting director has also been briefed on the situation, with Tyneside viewed as an attractive destination by those close to the player.

Atalanta view Scalvini as one of their most valuable assets and will not sell unless they receive an irresistable offer.

The £42m figure is the absolute minimum bid they would entertain.

Sports.title: Liverpool ‘make contact with AC Milan over transfer for ex-Chelsea star Fikayo Tomori’ after Joe Gomez injury blow
Sports.content:
FIKAYO TOMORI has caught Liverpool’s attention and they’re not stepping down.

The AC Milan defender has several English clubs interested, having bounced back from the 2024/25 season and it may be time for the Serie A giants to move him on.



Premier League newcomers Coventry City were among the first to flirt with a move, but they were sensationally snubbed by the 28-year-old.

But Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool are reportedly in search of an experienced central defender, with Joe Gomez sidelined through injury.



The Reds have already made an initial move to start talks, according to Tutto Juve.

And while everything is still in the early stages, the English star’s name has been added to the shortlist.

Reports suggest that costs are being worked out with room for manoeuvres being considered too before an official offer is made.

While Gomez is a major cause for concern at the start of the season, Jeremy Jacquet will add to the issue as the club remain cautious following his shoulder surgery.

Defenders Ibrahima Konate and Andrew Robertson have also both departed from the club this window.

Meanwhile, centre-back Giovanni Leoni and right-back Conor Bradley are still to make a return to pre-season training after their own injuries.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Tomori’s current deal is set to expire next year, but it is to be seen whether the Chelsea academy product will make a return to the Prem.

The former England international has starred in northern Italy for the past five years, making 214 appearances.

He lifted the Scudetto in 2022 and won the Supercoppa Italiana in 2025.

After a rotated 2024/25 campaign where he started just 22 league matches, Tomori logged 33 starts in Serie A during 2025/26.

Sports.title: Curtis Jones has blazing row with Liverpool star ‘over captain’s armband’ as Inter Milan ‘prepare £30m transfer offer’
Sports.content:
CURTIS Jones was at the centre of a heated on-pitch bust-up after Liverpool’s pre-season win over Wrexham, with the captain’s armband appearing to spark the fiery exchange.

The Reds midfielder was seen angrily confronting Dominik Szoboszlai after Thursday’s 1-0 victory at New York’s Yankee Stadium.



Kostas Tsimikas was then dragged into the argument before cameras caught the Greek defender throwing Liverpool’s captain’s armband onto the turf – videos which leaked across social media.

The trio were walking around the pitch applauding supporters when the confrontation erupted.



Jeremie Frimpong attempted to pull Jones away from the incident, but the Liverpool academy graduate continued exchanging words before members of the coaching staff eventually intervened.

It remains unclear exactly what triggered the dispute.

However, during the match Szoboszlai handed the captain’s armband to Tsimikas after being substituted instead of passing it to Jones.

That decision appeared to become a major talking point once the final whistle had blown.

Szoboszlai refused to reveal the cause of the row, but hinted that emotions are running high within the squad following a summer of major change including Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot as head coach.

The Hungarian midfielder said: “Now that a couple of guys have left and maybe we are not the oldest in the team but we’ve been here a long time, we are all in the same boat and we want the best for the club and for each other.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“We have a captain in Virgil [van Dijk] and we will follow him everywhere with what he and the gaffer says and I think I can talk from everybody’s side that we want to be successful this season.

“It’s a long term [project] because obviously we have a new manager and the team has been changed. Maybe not in a couple of months but in the long term, I think it will work out.”

The incident comes as Jones’ future continues to dominate headlines.

Inter Milan have renewed their pursuit of the 25-year-old after Liverpool rejected an opening offer worth around £21.7million earlier this summer.



The Athletic reports Inter have now indicated they are prepared to pay around €35million (£30m), although Liverpool continue to value Jones at closer to €40m.

With just one year remaining on his contract, Liverpool are reportedly prepared to risk losing Jones for free in 2027 rather than accept a fee below their valuation.

Jones has been with Liverpool since childhood and broke into the first team during the 2019/20 campaign, memorably scoring the winner against Everton in an FA Cup third-round tie at Anfield.

Although he has never fully nailed down a guaranteed starting place, Jones has remained an important squad player throughout Liverpool’s success – helping the club win two Premier League titles, the FA Cup and two Carabao Cups.



His consistent performances have also earned him six England caps.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Should he complete a move to Inter, Jones would join former Manchester City defender John Stones in Milan as the Serie A champions continue strengthening their squad ahead of the new campaign.

Liverpool’s next pre-season game will be against Leeds tomorrow in Chicago.

Sports.title: Man Utd star named on bench but sits in STANDS for Atletico Madrid friendly amid intense transfer interest
Sports.content:
ALTAY BAYINDIR was nowhere to be seen on the touchline after Manchester United beat Atletico Madrid this afternoon.

Bryan Mbeumo scored twice to come from behind as Man Utd secured a 2-1 friendly win over Atletico.



And despite the Turkish keeper being listed on the bench, he was sat in the STANDS as talks about his planned departure continue.

United have confirmed that the ace is expected to leave.



The 28-year-old’s agent was at United’s Carrington training facility on Wednesday to discuss Bayindir’s next steps.

He reported for pre-season training but United had already signed Karl Darlow from Leeds as their new back-up shot-stopper.

Besiktas was tipped in February as a possible destination for the former Fenerbache goalkeeper.

He has not started for the Red Devils since September last year when they lost 3-1 at Brentford.

And he only started six Premier League games. But he lost three of them.

From 17 appearances in a United shirt, Bayindir has conceded 31 goals, winning eight and losing seven.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In the friendly today, Arnau Ortiz handed the Spaniards an early lead after he buried a cross into the bottom corner.

Man Utd – wearing a royal blue number – saw a big chance as Shea Lacey’s ball found Mbeumo who got a glancing header on it, sending it just wide.

The Red Devils continued to knock at the door but failed to capitalise in the Strawberry Arena before the break.

Lacey’s magic continued in the second-half, winning United a penalty.



Mbeumo stepped up to the spot and sent the keeper the wrong way to coolly slot the ball into the bottom corner in the 53rd minute.

And it was Cameroon international who struck again as he found the roof of the net from close range to take the lead.

Sports.title: Bryan Mbeumo promises a ‘big’ season from Man Utd amid title challenge as he reveals no regrets over transfer
Sports.content:
BRYAN MBEUMO insists Manchester United are aiming “big” in the Premier League next season.

Mbeumo, 26, scored twice in United’s 2-1 pre-season win against Atletico Madrid as they retained the Snapdragon Cup in Stockholm.



Expectations have been raised at United ahead of the forthcoming campaign following their third-place finish last term.

Players have talked up a possible title challenge under Michael Carrick and Mbeumo is quietly confident of an even better second season at the club.



“I wasn’t surprised,” Mbeumo said when asked about the third-place finish. “Because it’s a big club and we always aim big and we worked a lot to be there, so I wasn’t surprised.

“We always try to give the best that we can on the pitch and work really hard, so we will see and try our best.”



Mbeumo, a winger, has scored all of his goals under Carrick whilst playing up front and added two more against Atletico from the centre forward role.

Carrick dropped Joshua Zirkzee and moved Mbeumo further forward, with rookie Shea Lacey starring in the No10 role and the returning Amad on the right wing.

Mbeumo added: “Obviously, I’m lucky to be able to play a different position and I try to give my best. It depends on the games (where I play).

“We try to get ready for the first game of the season and we work really hard on the training so it’s really important to have good results as well.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“(Lacey’s) a young player with good abilities and is working hard, so happy to have him.”

Tottenham and Newcastle both wanted Mbeumo last year before he moved to United from Brentford in a £71million deal.

United were unhappy with Brentford during discussions and felt that they attempted to pressure Mbeumo into moving to Spurs or Newcastle.

Tottenham finished a place above the relegation zone while Newcastle came 12th and have already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, with Bruno Guimaraes also set to join Arsenal.

Mbeumo unsurprisingly has no regrets about opting for United, saying: “Obviously I’m always really challenging myself every time and will never regret having this challenge.”

Sports.title: Altay Bayindir on verge of leaving Man Utd as Everton make shock transfer enquiry for youngster
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is on the verge of leaving the club after three years.

Bayindir, 28, sat in the stands during United’s friendly with Atletico Madrid at the Strawberry Arena in Stockholm even though he was listed as a substitute.



The Turkey international participated in the warm-up with fellow ‘keepers Tom Heaton, Radek Vitek and Dermot Mee but was not on the bench.

Celta Vigo want to sign Bayindir on loan but another club that has shown interest wants the back-up goalie permanently.



Bayindir’s agent held further talks with United about a transfer earlier this week.

United signed Bayindir for £4.1million from Fenerbahce on deadline day in September 2023 but he has conceded 31 goals in 17 appearances.



Heaton played the full 90 minutes against Atletico but Senne Lammens is expected back in goal against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg next week after he reported for pre-season a few days ago.

United signed Karl Darlow to provide cover for Lammens but he is still out following a procedure that took place at the end of last season.

Former Leeds United goalkeeper Darlow, 35, is due to be available for the start of the new season.

Everton have also contacted United about the possibility of a move for 20-year-old striker Ethan Wheatley, who was dropped from the squad against Atletico and Rosenborg last week.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Wheatley has had spells on loan at Walsall, Northampton Town and Bradford City in League One in the past two years, mustering only three goals.

He has made four substitute appearances for United but the academy graduate could make the surprising switch to Everton’s academy.

Championship clubs have also been in contact with United about Wheatley, who is under contract until 2028.

Everton have issues up front with Beto and Thierno Barry both unconvincing but Wheatley would not be considered a first-team recruit.

The former United academy head Nick Cox joined Everton as technical director last year.

Sports.title: Danny Welbeck completes Chelsea transfer on 2-year deal as he’s spotted at empty training ground with squad in Australia
Sports.content:
DANNY WELBECK has been unveiled as Chelsea’s latest signing.

The former Brighton man, 35, has penned a two-year deal as he looks set to join Xabi Alonso‘s squad for their pre-season tour.



Welbeck’s deal with the Seagulls was set to expire next summer but the seaside outfit agreed on the move to the capital for an undisclosed fee.

In a statement on the club’s website, Welbeck said: “When you hear of the interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride.



“Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time.



“I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection.

“I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Welbeck had a box office campaign last time around, scoring a career-high of 13 Premier League goals as he helped Brighton secure eighth spot and Conference League football.

The England international will arrive in west London already with 400 Prem appearances under his belt, as well as Champions League experience.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Under Sir Alex Ferguson, Welbeck finished top of the league, lifted the League Cup twice, and won the Club World Cup in 2008.

From Manchester United, the ace made the journey to Arsenal in September 2014.

And he stayed for the next five seasons, scoring 32 goals in 126 appearances and winning the FA Cup and Community Shield.

Then former Watford ace is the latest addition at Stamford Bridge following the record-breaking signing of Morgan Rogers, as well as Maxence Lacroix, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra and striker Emmanuel Emegha.



The Man Utd academy product will now board the plane to Hong Kong to link up with the rest of the Chelsea squad as they continue their pre-season odyssey.

Sports.title: Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return
Sports.content:
Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return

Mykhailo Mudryk can officially return to football, and his Chelsea team-mates have made their feelings perfectly clear

View 2 Images Levi Colwill was one of many Chelsea stars to send a message to Mykhailo Mudryk (Image: (Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images))

Several Chelsea stars have issued messages of support to Mykhailo Mudryk after his doping ban was lifted. The 25-year-old has not played for the Blues since November 2024 after testing positive for meldonium and being handed a four-year suspension by the FA

‌



Earlier this week, a statement was released by English football's governing body which stated that that disciplinary proceedings against the Ukrainian had been resolved. A provisional ban was placed on Mudryk a month on from his failed test.

‌



During his time out, an appeal was lodged with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while confirmation of a hearing being set arrived in May of last year with 'written submissions' also exchanged. However, the situation has now been resolved with Mudryk posting on social media after the decision was made official.

‌



Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso gives Mykhailo Mudryk update as winger handed green light to return READ MORE :

His Chelsea team-mates Levi Colwill and Reece James led tributes by reposting his official statement to their Instagram stories. Romeo Lavia, Nicolas Jackson, Robert Sanchez, and Malo Gusto all followed their lead.

Meanwhile, former teammates including Ben Chilwell, Marc Cucurella, and Christopher Nkunku, alongside Cole Palmer, Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo, Pedro Neto, and Wesley Fofana, were amongst the 1.5 million users to 'like' the Ukrainian's post.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Almost 60,000 users also flooded the comment section with messages of support. It is understood that Mudryk will now travel to Hong Kong to link up with the Chelsea squad ahead of Wednesday's friendly against Juventus.

Speaking to journalists at the Accor Stadium in Sydney, Australia, on Saturday, following a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur, Alonso described the winger as a 'special' player, while tempering expectations regarding any immediate return to action.

"We are happy for him, especially for him," said the Blues manager. "Probably, we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time and how does he feel at the moment with the things that he had to cope with.

‌



"We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the teammates, from the staff, and for sure it will take time. So once he is with us, we will see how things develop."

On Mudryk's future, Alonso said: "We need to see, it's too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it's still early to tell."

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso's latest Chelsea press conference was dominated by Mykhailo Mudryk

‌



The Chelsea boss added: "We have the Mudryk that [we had], it will take time, but once there is a change, things start moving, and for him it's a massive change. So he trained on his own every day, and I think it had to be really, really hard, because he wanted to play football.

"He wanted to be part of a team, and he was not allowed to do that for such a long time. So once this big change has happened, now things will move on, and afterwards we will see if it's quicker, if it's slower, but we need to be aware of that."

Reflecting on Mudryk's abilities as a footballer, Alonso said: "Yeah, I remember watching him in Shakhtar, the impact he had, how quick he is, how good in one-on-one situations, how he could create a lot of situations on his own, and he's a special player, but he will take time for sure."

Article continues below

"To be honest, we were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy. We feel that he will be working with us."

Sports.title: West Ham break silence on ownership after Amanda Staveley’s consortium 'agrees 25% stake'
Sports.content:
West Ham break silence on ownership after Amanda Staveley’s consortium 'agrees 25% stake'

West Ham United have released a statement which throws the future of the club ownership into doubt, and leaves them in limbo until after the summer transfer window shuts

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is reported to have agreed a deal for a 25 per cent stake in West Ham (Image: Anthony Devlin/Getty Images for IWG)

A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United. Since news broke on Saturday afternoon, the Championship club have given an update in an official statement.

‌



The move comes after the family of the late David Gold agreed to sell 16 per cent of their stake to Royal Mail owner Daniel Kretinsky earlier this summer. It, however, has emerged that Staveley's consortium offered a higher price to buy the full Gold stake.

‌



Staveley’s intervention comes weeks after David Sullivan, 77, resigned as West Ham co-chairman in June after allegations of sexual abuse were reported by a Times and BBC Panorama investigation. Sullivan denies the allegations, calling them “factually incorrect and entirely false”.

‌



As things stand, Staveley or Kretinsky would still need to buy Sullivan's 38.8 per cent share to take majority control of the club.

In a club statement, released on Saturday evening, the Hammers said: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from Joint-Chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the Club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation.

"Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

‌



"The Club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."

Staveley is known in English football for leading the Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund's takeover of Newcastle United. She left her role as a director at the club in 2024.

The consortium who have agreed a deal for the stake in West Ham is led by Staveley, alongside her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and their firm PCP Capital Partners. They are said to be in partnership with the American private investment firm Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

‌



View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is the former co-owner of Newcastle United (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Following the twist, a spokesperson for Krentinsky, who still owns 27 per cent of the club, told The Times: “The agreement we had reached with the Gold family in June provided stability for the club at a crucial time.

“This does the opposite. We will always act in the best interests of West Ham United and are reviewing all of our options, including exercising our pre-emption rights in full.”

‌



Meanwhile, representative of the Gold family, Vanessa Gold, said: “On the 12th of June Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led my Amanda Staeley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League."

Article continues below

West Ham suffered relegation to the Championship at the end of last season. They start their bid for an immediate return on Sunday, August 15, when they travel to take on fellow relegation sufferers Burnley at Turf Moor.

As things stand, no new faces have been brought in by the club as yet in the transfer market. However, West Ham have done some strong business by collecting around £155m for Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville combined, and they have managed to keep Jarrod Bowen at the London Stadium.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's plea boosts brain disease campaign led by England legend Nobby Stiles' son
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's plea boosts brain disease campaign led by England legend Nobby Stiles' son

EXCLUSIVE: Just before he died, Kevin Keegan spoke to Nobby Stiles' son, John, and encouraged him to push on with a campaign for a fund to be established to help with the cost of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy

View 4 Images Kevin Keegan, who played 63 times for England, sent John Stiles a message of support

Retired footballers face being struck down with a brain disease at epidemic levels, campaigners warn.

‌



John Stiles, 62, son of 1966 World Cup legend Nobby Stiles, is calling for a fund to help with the cost of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) due to heading the ball.

‌



Kevin Keegan sent him a message just before the Newcastle legend’s tragic death from cancer, telling him: “Keep fighting, John." Former Leeds man Stiles said ex-England boss Keegan was one of the key voices highlighting CTE.

‌



The brain disease has claimed the lives not only of John’s dad but also other players, including Scotland legend Gordon McQueen, former England and West Brom striker Jeff Astle and Chris Nicholl, the ex-Aston Villa and Northern Ireland player.

Funeral director Robert Bush who hoarded bodies and gave wrong ashes jailed READ MORE :

Chelsea hit with £10m fine and suspended transfer ban after Roman Abramovich breaches READ MORE :

View 4 Images John Stiles with a photo of his late dad, the Man Utd and England great Nobby Stiles (Image: Mirrorpix)

A coroner ruled Nobby died as a result of repeatedly heading the ball, which he did around 136,000 times in his career.

‌



Even John’s grandson George, 12, is aware of CTE and apologised for heading the ball to stop a goal in a recent junior game. John, from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, warned the future impact on players could be unprecedented.

He said: "We need a proper fund like the one in America, which had $1.5billion; the £1million fund set up by the FA and PL (Premier League) is just a stunt. It’s an insult. At the moment, the families are funding the treatment of ex-pros, and the taxpayer is covering costs through the benefits system, which is wrong.

“There are at least 55,000 ex-footballers in England. Research suggests there could be 16,500 to 27,500 footballers withdementia. That is as scandal. The boom in the women’s game is a real concern for me."

‌



View 4 Images John Stiles with a photo of his late dad, the Man Utd and England great Nobby Stiles

Norbert “Nobby” Stiles died in 2020, aged 78. His family had to sell his medals to help pay for his care.

Born in Collyhurst, Manchester, in 1942, he made 395 appearances for United between 1960 and 1971 and earned 28 England caps.

‌



He played every minute during the legendary 1966 World Cup campaign, despite his own concerns that he was going to be dropped after the Argentina game.

View 4 Images John Stiles with his dad Nobby at a dinner alongside 1966 England star Martin Peters

An FA Spokesperson said: "While the link between heading in football and long-term brain health remains the subject of ongoing scientific and medical research, we have consistently been at the forefront of efforts to help improve the safety of our game.

Article continues below

"We have led the way in this area to proactively review and strengthen player welfare across every level of English football, working closely with our domestic and international stakeholders.

"We were the first governing body to introduce comprehensive heading guidelines across both professional and grassroots football, and we continue to review and enhance our game-wide concussion protocols in line with worldwide best practice.

"We have also invested in and actively supported multiple independent research projects, often resulting in groundbreaking and valuable insight, in order to gain a greater understanding of this complex area through objective, robust and thorough analysis."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win

Manchester United beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sweden on Saturday in a match which offered plenty of clues to the club's transfer plans

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's squad for the 2026/27 season isn't settled yet (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick offered a telling hint towards his plans for the summer transfer window through his starting line-up against Atletico Madrid on Saturday.

‌



United came from behind to beat the Spanish side 2-1 in Sweden thanks to two goals from Bryan Mbeumo. The Cameroon international scored from the penalty spot to make it 1-1 after Shea Lacey was fouled before bundling in a second from Jack Fletcher's low cross.

‌



There were plenty of encouraging signs for Carrick, who has also overseen a 5-0 win over Rosenborg and a 1-0 defeat by Wrexham so far in pre-season. Further friendlies are scheduled against Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds and AC Milan before United begin their 2026/27 campaign against newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

‌



United have used the summer transfer window to recruit Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, while a handful of players have left already. But it's clear that there is still more work to do, and that the current squad on pre-season tour isn't the one Carrick wants to start the campaign with.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points READ MORE :

Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear READ MORE :

There were two changes to the starting XI from the United boss, with Radek Vitek and Joshua Zirkzee dropping out for Tom Heaton and Amad. Zirkzee scored and assisted in the thrashing of Rosenborg, yet only got 17 minutes as a substitute against Atletico Madrid, with Carrick prioritising playing time for others.

‌



The Dutch striker is on the transfer list and United hope to find a buyer for a player who has managed just nine goals in 75 appearances since making a £36.5million move to Old Trafford two years ago. Juventus are reportedly interested in Zirkzee, whose future is currently up in the air.

Vitek's status in the squad is clear, with United signing Darlow on a free transfer to become Senne Lammens' back-up. The 22-year-old impressed on loan with Bristol City last season and has no shortage of suitors, although his £10m valuation is yet to be reached. United are keen to cash in and reinvest the cash elsewhere.

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir was not involved against Atletico Madrid (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, Altay Bayindir was not involved at all against Atleti, with Heaton, Vitek and youngster Dermot Mee the three goalkeepers chosen by Carrick. Bayindir conducted a training session prior the game in Stockholm before taking a seat behind the dugout to watch proceedings.

Manchester Evening News reports that Bayindir is keen to leave United this summer to find regular minutes and that Celta Vigo are keen to sign the Turkey international on a season-long loan deal, while a Turkish side could sign him permanently.

Bayindir has made just 17 appearances for United since joining for £4.3m in 2023. He played second fiddle to Andre Onana initially before Lammens' arrival last season made it clear he wouldn't get a chance as No.1.

Sports.content:

Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley had two loan spells in League One last season and now the young star is reportedly attracting Premier League interest

View 2 Images Man Utd striker Ethan Wheatley is being linked with Everton (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Everton are reportedly preparing a transfer approach for Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley. However, it is understood that nothing is advanced at this stage.

The 20-year-old ended last season on loan at League One side Bradford City after spending the first half of the campaign with Northampton Town. The Red Devils youngster made 12 appearances for the Bantams in 2025/26 as he sought more senior first-team football.

Sports.title: Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost
Sports.content:
Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost

Arsenal are hoping to sign Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes this summer, with a possible hint at their confidence in a deal

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is looking to stregthen his Arsenal squad ahead of the new season. (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal have reached an agreement to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton, in a hint over their confidence in completing a deal for Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazilian is a key transfer target for Arsenal this summer.

‌



As reported by the Liverpool ECHO, Arsenal have agreed a fee in the region of £7million with Everton over the sale of Norgaard. A medical is due to take place next week, ahead of the move being finalised.

‌



Norgaard only joined Arsenal last summer, but found game time hard to come by at the Emirates Stadium. Last season saw him make just seven appearances in the Premier League, with a further 18 coming in all other competitions.

‌



New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer READ MORE :

Despite the lack of game time, selling the midfielder indicates that Arsenal expect more additions in the position, with Guimaraes emerging as a priority addition. Arsenal's interest in the Newcastle midfielder comes at a time of chaos at St James' Park.

It was confirmed this week that Eddie Howe has left his position as Newcastle boss. It was reported that his decision to leave the club was partly due to the possibility of Guimaraes being sold this summer, following the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

‌



Incoming boss Matthias Jaissle is expected to hold face-to-face talks with Guimaraes. The chat will see him try to sell his vision and philosophy.

However, it is expected that the two clubs will reach an agreement over a fee in the coming days. The transfer fee is expected to be at least £80million, possibly up to £85million with add-ons.

‌



If an exit for Norgaard, and a transfer for Guimaraes is sealed, then the Brazilian will add to Mikel Arteta's midfield options. Martin Odegaard is club captain and is joined by Martin Zubimendi, Declan Rice and Mikel Merino, with three of the four players still on their extended break following their success in the World Cup.

The talk over Norgaard's future comes after he made a promise last October. Speaking to Danish outlet Bold, he said: "I can guarantee that Arsenal will be my last club abroad.

“I still want to return to Brondby when my contract at Arsenal expires. My contract is two years with an option for a further year.
